Distribution. — Hŋlodes caete is known from the crests and slopes in high montane, montane, and submontane dense ombrophilous forests of Serra do Mar in the State of São Paulo (Figs. 6 and 7). The new species is known to occur in the municipalities of Pilar do Sul, Ibiúna, Itanhaém, São Vicente, Santos, Cubatão, Santo André (Paranapiacaba), and São Paulo (Fig. 7). The new species is sympatric and syntopic with H. phŋllodes. We recorded these two species together at the type locality and in the municipalities of São Vicente, Santos, Cubatão, and Santo André (Paranapiacaba) of the State of São Paulo. Moreover, we recorded synchronotopic calling activity of the two species in the type locality (Fig. 8 A; also see audio files associated with the Supplemental Materials available online). Advertisement call. — The advertisement call of H. caete has harmonic structure and the first harmonic is not apparent (Fig. 8 B). At 20.8 – 22.8 ° C air temperature and 19.2 – 21 ° C water temperature, call duration ranges from 1.22 – 2.72 s (1.79 ± 0.38 s, n ¼ 36 calls from 6 males); calls occur at intervals ranging from 1.85 – 7.72 s (3.54 ± 1.19 s, n ¼ 36 intervals from 6 males); 20 – 45 notes per call (30 ± 6.67, n ¼ 36 calls from 6 males), given at a rate ranging from 14.8 – 18.3 / s (16.6 ± 1.02 / s, n ¼ 36 calls from 6 males); note duration ranges from 0.009 – 0.023 s (0.016 ± 0.002 s, n ¼ 108 notes of 36 calls from 6 males); notes given at intervals ranging from 0.036 – 0.058 s (0.45 ± 0.005 s, n ¼ 108 intervals of 36 calls from 6 males); each note consists of a rising frequency – modulated whistle; the dominant frequency occurs in the third harmonic and ranges from 3937.5 – 5062.5 Hz (4640.63 ± 28.47 Hz, n ¼ 36 call notes from 6 males); the first note may be lower, with a dominant frequency range of 3937.5 – 4687.5 Hz (4283.7 ± 18.01, n ¼ 36 call notes from 6 males).

Distribution and ecology. The new species is currently only known from Tuoniang River Basin (upper reach of the You River) in Yunnan and Guangxi, a sub-basin in the upper Pearl River system (Fig. 3). Molecular phylogeny Both phylogenetic methods (ML and BI) recovered a similar tree in topology (Fig. 4), based on two mitochondrial gene fragments (Cyt b, CO I) and also consistent with the results reported by Jiang et al. (2011). Species with dark brown to dark yellow body and black saddle-like patches beneath the dorsal and adipose fin formed a distinct monophyletic clade (in green), represented by Glyptothorax hainanensis, G. honghensis and G. sinensis. Species with a dark body and creamy or bright yellow spots or stripes formed another distinct monophyletic clade (in orange), represented by Glyptothorax pulcher sp. nov., G. quadriocellatus and G. pallozonum. The monophyly of the new species is strongly supported. Phylogenetic evidence indicated that G. pulcher is closely related to G. pallozonum, both of which are from the Pearl River, the estimated K 2 P genetic distances between the two range from 5.7 % to 6.0 % (Table 3).
